Role Summary

We're looking for a Principal Engineer to architect, fine-tune, and deploy on-device small language models (SLMs) for consumer security at scale. You will serve as the technical authority for AI/ML initiatives, driving architecture, model development, optimization, and deployment while collaborating with engineering teams across the organization.

Your core responsibility is building high-performance, privacy-preserving AI models that run directly on user devices (Mac, iOS, Android, Linux). You’ll own model optimization, fine-tuning for tool-use accuracy, evaluation frameworks, and cost-aware deployment strategies. While you won’t own the agent orchestration platform itself, you’ll work closely with it to ensure models behave correctly in multi-turn conversations and make reliable tool-calling decisions. 

This role sits at the intersection of edge ML, applied LLMs, and production engineering. Success requires navigating real-world tradeoffs: latency vs. capability, privacy vs. accuracy, on-device vs. cloud execution, and cost vs. performance. 

This is a Hybrid position located in a hub location of Frisco, TX, San Jose, CA, Newport Beach, CA, or New York, NY. You will be required to be onsite on an as-needed basis, typically 1-4 days per month. We are only considering candidates within a commutable distance to this location and are not offering relocation assistance at this time.

Position Details

About The Role

Design and deploy small language models optimized for on-device inference (Mac, iOS, Android, Linux)
Lead model optimization efforts including quantization, pruning, distillation, and efficient inference pipelines
Fine-tune models to improve tool selection accuracy and conversational behavior in security-focused workflows
Build evaluation frameworks to measure model efficacy, tool-calling accuracy, conversation quality, and safety in production
Create synthetic data and workflow simulations to train and validate security-relevant conversations
Partner closely with agent orchestration systems to optimize multi-turn dialogue behavior and state handling
Implement cost-optimization strategies such as intelligent on-device vs. cloud routing, prompt caching, batching, and token efficiency
Integrate cloud-based LLMs when deeper reasoning or broader context is required
Build production ML systems that detect threats and protect users directly on-device
Set technical standards and architectural direction for AI/ML across the security platform 
Influence engineers, architects, and technical leaders through design reviews, technical guidance, and engineering best practices.
Design and maintain scalable AI evaluation harnesses that enable automated testing, benchmarking, and regression detection across model quality, tool-calling behavior, safety, and production workflows.
Develop red-team testing frameworks and adversarial evaluation methodologies to measure and improve model robustness, security, and resiliency against emerging threat scenarios.
Build reusable AI engineering platforms, tooling, and infrastructure that accelerate model experimentation, evaluation, deployment, and operational monitoring across multiple teams and products.

About You

10+ years of software engineering experience, with 5+ years focused on ML/AI
Proven experience shipping ML models to production with transferrable skills to deploy these on edge or mobile platforms
Experience with conversational AI systems and tool/function-calling architectures
Strong Python and systems programming skills (C++ or Rust) for performance-critical code
Drive cross-functional technical initiatives that span multiple products and engineering organizations.
Deep expertise in model optimization (INT4/INT8 quantization, pruning, distillation)
Hands-on experience with PyTorch and at least one edge deployment framework (TensorFlow Lite, CoreML, ONNX Runtime, or llama.cpp)
Experience building evaluation and benchmarking frameworks for ML systems
Experience applying ML systems in security, safety, or other adversarial domains

added.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, AI Safety Evaluations
added.description:
NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Realizing that potential means answering some of the hardest questions in AI: Where do models fall short? Which risks are we missing? How do we know our safeguards are working? As an expert in machine learning for Evaluations, you’ll help establish the evidence that guides the next generation of safer AI. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next.

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Researcher / Data Scientist to join our AI Safety and Responsibility efforts within Enterprise Risk Management. Engaging directly in engineering tasks, you will apply your data science and statistics skills. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like.

What You Will Be Doing

Safety Benchmarking: Design and maintain safety benchmarks for large language and multimodal models, translating risk scenarios into test cases, datasets, and scoring rubrics.
Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise.
Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases.
Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment.
Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues.
Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers.

What We Need To See

Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation.
Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty. Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments.
Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows.
Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence.
Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming.
Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks.
Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues.
Human-Aligned Evaluation: Experience validating model-based evaluators against human judgments or designing human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows.
Statistical Rigor: Strong model evaluation skills and a commitment to sound statistical practices, including confidence intervals.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Do you enjoy building impactful AI agents and agentic applications? Join the GenAI/ML Specialist organization as a Senior Generative AI Data Scientist — a senior individual contributor role requiring deep data science expertise, hands-on ML engineering skills, and executive-level customer engagement.

The AGS Specialist organization is part of the customer-facing NAMER sales organization, and is responsible for driving revenue and accelerating adoption of cloud and partner services across diverse customer segments. We work backwards from our customers' most complex and business-critical challenges to develop and execute go-to-market plans that transform ideas into scalable, high-impact businesses. AGS NAMER teams include sales specialists and technical solution architects. As part of the team, you will contribute across the full lifecycle of AWS customer initiatives—from shaping new service and solution concepts to accelerating adoption of established offerings. We pride ourselves on thinking big, delivering exceptional customer outcomes, and collaborating seamlessly across AWS as #OneTeam.

Role Description

In this role, you will be the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for helping NAMER Enterprise customers design and implement Generative AI solutions that leverage Amazon Bedrock. You will translate customer business challenges into data science-driven solutions using AWS. You will define, design, and deploy machine learning models, agentic workflows, and GenAI applications that accelerate adoption of AWS AI/ML services. You will engage with senior engineers, data scientists, product leaders, and executives at strategic enterprise customers to influence technical decisions and provide structured feedback to AWS product teams.

You will interact with customers directly to understand their business problems, help and aid them in implementation of generative AI solutions, deliver briefings and deep dive sessions, and guide customers on adoption patterns and best practices for generative AI. You will build prototypes, proof-of-concepts, and explore novel solutions leveraging Amazon Bedrock, Amazon AgentCore, Strands Agents, and open source frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, and CrewAI.

This position will focus on agentic workflows with Amazon Bedrock, including Strands Agents, Bedrock Agents, and open source agentic frameworks. You must have deep technical experience working with technologies related to large language models including LLM architectures, model evaluation, and fine-tuning techniques. You should be proficient with design, deployment, and evaluation of LLM-powered agents, tools, and orchestration approaches.

You will interface with customer data science teams, ML engineering leadership, and C-suite executives to advise on the latest techniques, model architectures, and emerging research. This includes staying current with state-of-the-art approaches from recent publications and research papers — such as advances in reasoning models, multi-agent systems, retrieval-augmented generation, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), and novel fine-tuning methods — and translating those findings into practical, production-ready solutions for enterprise customers. You will lead technical deep dives and whiteboard sessions with customer chief data scientists and VPs of AI/ML, bridging the gap between research and real-world implementation on AWS.

You should understand the security and compliance requirements for ML/GenAI implementations. You should have experience architecting end-to-end ML/GenAI agentic applications for customers using AWS services and the Well-Architected Framework.

As the ideal candidate, you bring a deep data science background and the business acumen required to lead complex engagements with large enterprises. You have hands-on expertise in statistical modeling, traditional ML, and current areas such as LLMs, RAG, fine-tuning, AI system evaluation, prompt engineering, agents, and AIOps. You are able to credibly advise senior technical and executive stakeholders on architectural trade-offs, best practices, and risk mitigation.

Key job responsibilities

Working with NAMER Enterprise customers' development and data science teams to deeply understand their business and technical needs. Design and implement solutions that make the best use of the AWS cloud platform and AWS AI/ML services including SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon AgentCore, and other AI/ML services.
Customer Advisor — Implement and deploy state-of-the-art machine learning and Generative AI solutions. Build prototypes, PoCs, and explore new solutions. Interact closely with enterprise customers to accelerate their AI/ML adoption.
Partner with Data Scientists, SAs, Sales, Business Development, and the AI/ML Service teams to accelerate customer adoption and revenue attainment in NAMER for Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and related services that support GenAI use cases.
Thought Leadership – Evangelize AWS GenAI services and share best practices through forums such as AWS blogs, whitepapers, reference architectures, and public-speaking events such as AWS Summit, AWS re:Invent, etc.
Act as a technical liaison between customers and the Amazon Bedrock or other service teams to provide customer-driven product improvement feedback.
Develop and support an AWS internal community of GenAI-related subject matter experts in the AMERICAS. Create field enablement materials for the broader technical population, to help them understand how to integrate AWS GenAI solutions into customer architectures.

A day in the life

Your day will be dynamic and impactful. You'll engage with enterprise business leaders, dive deep into ML architectures and data science pipelines, and craft transformative AI strategies. You'll collaborate across teams, translating complex statistical and AI concepts into clear, actionable solutions that drive meaningful business outcomes for NAMER Enterprise customers.

About The Team

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

At Franklin Templeton, we believe success is built through powerful partnerships. As a forward thinking asset manager, we build dynamic relationships with clients, understand their goals, and navigate complex markets together. We leverage cutting edge strategies and deep insights to unlock opportunities for long term wealth creation. Our talented, global teams bring expertise that is both broad and unique.

From our welcoming, inclusive, and supportive culture to our globally diverse business, we offer opportunities not only to help you reach your potential, but also to contribute to our clients’ success.

Forward Deployed AI Engineer

About The Department

Forward Deployed AI Engineers embed with priority Technology teams to solve real delivery problems using AI-enabled engineering practices. They work alongside developers and technical leads to improve outcomes while transferring capabilities back to the host team.

Each engagement should leave the team more capable, with reusable context, tools, and practices. The role also strengthens the broader enablement model by turning field lessons into improvements to the internal delivery-guidance product, AI PDLC, education, and reuse ecosystem.

How You Will Add Value

Embed with Technology teams in bounded engagements to identify opportunities, establish baselines, deliver against agreed outcomes, and transfer ownership.
Learn the host team’s codebase, architecture, delivery practices, data constraints, quality standards, and governance obligations.
Help teams create AI-ready context: repository and documentation evidence, team conventions, approved boundaries, decision rights, and questions requiring human escalation.
Configure and use AI workspaces, harnesses, skills, instructions, evaluation assets, and workflow patterns suited to the team’s goals.
Build or adapt agentic workflows, retrieval patterns, tools, structured outputs, evaluations, and observability practices that improve delivery without weakening quality or control.
Apply the AI PDLC across all aspects of software design and delivery.
Pair with engineers and technical leads as a constructive team member. Earn trust through useful contribution, give credit generously, and respect local expertise.
Measure outcomes such as lead time, engineering effort, rework, defects, governance exceptions, developer friction, and capacity released.
Capture proven practices and unresolved gaps; turn them into specific feedback and reusable assets for product, research, governance, education, and community partners.

What Will Help You Be Successful In This Role

The host team can continue and extend the work independently, with clearer context for its AI tools and evidence of improved productivity, quality, control, or developer experience. The engineer also improves the system beyond that team: reusable patterns are documented, product feedback is actionable, and the next engagement starts from a stronger base.

Eight to ten years of relevant experience, including leading technically complex delivery work and influencing practices beyond a single team.
Strong software engineering ability and the capacity to contribute quickly in unfamiliar codebases.
Hands-on AI engineering experience. Relevant examples include Python or TypeScript; APIs; cloud platforms; Git and CI/CD; containers; retrieval; tool use; agentic workflows; prompt and context engineering; structured outputs; and evaluation.
Ability to build and use AI harnesses: reusable instructions, skills, tools, context files, test cases, evaluation suites, traces, observability, and human-review checkpoints.
Product and business curiosity; able to distinguish a practical intervention from an attractive technical demonstration.
Analytical and communication skills: form hypotheses, establish baselines, measure outcomes, adapt based on evidence, and explain technical work clearly.
Collaborative, low-ego behavior: earns trust, gives credit, shares useful tools, and leaves teams stronger.

Preferred Experience

Forward deployment, consulting, solutions engineering, platform engineering, developer productivity, or technical product implementation.
AI evaluation, safety, monitoring, alignment, or model-risk practices.
Financial services or another regulated environment.
Reusable libraries, open-source contributions, internal tools, playbooks, technical writing, training, or community leadership.

Job Summary:

Core Experiences includes payments, requests, the social feed, notifications, search, and network growth. CFS includes products such as the Venmo debit card and funds-in. Commerce focuses on business payments and helping merchants grow.

As a senior data science leader, you’ll help shape Venmo’s growth strategy by finding and sizing opportunities and deciding what to measure, test, and build. You’ll partner with business, product, engineering, risk, and other teams, and develop scalable approaches to experimentation and measurement, including causal inference, social and network effects, forecasting, and engagement. Lead data science for your area, setting the analytical strategy and ensuring timely delivery aligned with product and business goals.
Design and analyze complex experiments, including tests where one person's experience affects their friends, tests in a two-sided network, and tests with small samples or long-term outcomes, and define the guardrails that protect payments and trust.
Define the metrics, funnels, and models that follow people and businesses from first use to lasting engagement, including activation, retention, and healthy engagement for a payments app.

Build and own AI-native data science workflows: agents, skills and context layers for instrumentation, analysis, experiment readouts and data quality checks, with clear boundaries between trusted automation and expert judgment.
Measure the quality and impact of AI and agentic product experiences, combining product metrics with model-quality and evaluation signals.
Help lead how AI makes data science faster at Venmo, from instrumentation to analysis and data quality checks.

Experience with consumer financial products or analytics for payments, cards, deposits, or credit, or with merchant and small business analytics.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
About Autopoiesis Sciences

We're building AI capable of autonomous scientific discovery. Our mission is to reach a world where discovery is no longer bottlenecked by the number of human scientists alive to pursue it.

Reinforcement learning has taken models remarkably far in math and code, where an answer can be checked and a model can learn from ten thousand attempts. Science offers no such reward function. The judgment a scientist exercises before any result is certain, which hypothesis is worth the month, what the evidence actually supports, when to abandon a promising dead end, has never been captured at scale. That missing signal is the real bottleneck, and it's the one we build for: the environments, datasets, and expert reasoning that teach models to do science, not just recite it.

That work is already in the world. We built and operate Aristotle, an AI research partner trusted by thousands of researchers at some of the most demanding institutions in science, including GSK, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, Merck, Stanford, MIT, Harvard, and the FDA. Alongside it, we're developing autonomous research systems that take on long-horizon scientific problems end to end.

Backed by leading investors and advised by the scientists who built the field, Autopoiesis is redefining what discovery looks like in the most important industry of the century.

About the role

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to put autonomous R&D inside the world's most demanding enterprises. Our newest system takes on research problems over days and weeks, works across an organization's data and tools, and acts on its own. Almost no one has deployed anything like it, and the playbook is still being written. You'll write a good part of it.

You'll work directly with R&D teams at our customers to understand how their research really runs, where their data lives, and what they would and wouldn't trust a system to do unsupervised. The job is to decide what to build for each deployment, what belongs in the core product for everyone, and what to say no to. You'll ship in days, not quarters, and what you learn in the field will shape what the rest of the company builds.

There's a second reason this role matters. Every deployment shows us where autonomy earns trust and where it breaks. That is the signal our mission depends on, and you'll be the person closest to it.

This is a role that calls for someone who has been through it before. You've shipped software into an environment you didn't control and debugged it live with the customer's IT team. You've told a senior scientist, or a senior executive, that their idea wouldn't work, explained why, and kept their trust. You're a strong engineer who can go from a messy dataset to a working integration without waiting for a spec, and you're comfortable making the call when the right answer isn't obvious and no one is available to ask. You'll be trusted to make those calls on your own, in the room, on the customer's time.

Key responsibilities

Own customer deployments end to end. Take each customer from signed contract to daily use, including scoping, integration, rollout, and the unglamorous work of getting teams to rely on a system that works autonomously.
Build what the customer needs. Write the connectors, workflows, and integrations that connect our system to a customer's data, tools, and methods, from internal databases and lab systems to domain-specific pipelines.
Define how autonomy works in the enterprise. Work with each customer to set what the system can access, what it can do on its own, and where a human stays in the loop, and design the controls, oversight, and audit trails that make those boundaries real.
Turn the field into product. Separate what is unique to one customer from what is true for all of them, and bring the second kind back to engineering with evidence, prototypes, and a clear argument for why it matters.
Earn customers' trust. Measure whether the system is producing real value, show the results to the people who decide renewals, and be honest when it isn't. Be the engineer our customers ask for by name.

Preferred qualifications

Experience as a forward deployed, solutions, or customer-facing engineer at a fast-growing AI, data, or developer-tools company, where you shipped real software inside customer environments, not just demos.
Strong software engineering fundamentals, especially Python, data pipelines, APIs, and integrating with systems you didn't design.
Hands-on experience building with LLMs and autonomous agents, including evaluating whether they work on a customer's actual problem and not just on a benchmark.
A track record of taking a deployment from a skeptical pilot to expanded, durable usage.
Experience deploying into enterprise environments with real constraints, including private cloud, VPC, or on-prem, and working through a customer's security and IT review.
Comfort with ambiguity and with owning an outcome across product, engineering, and the customer, with no one handing you a ticket.
Familiarity with scientific or industrial R&D, such as biology, chemistry, materials, or clinical research, or genuine curiosity about how research gets done.

Our values

The mission is the only thing.
Everything we do either moves discovery forward or it doesn't, and anything that doesn't is a day we won't get back. We hold every decision, every hire, and every week against that one question. The mission is hard enough that nothing else earns a place next to it.

Bet on the process, not the outcome.
We think in expected value. A good decision made on the best available information is a good decision even when the result disappoints, and a lucky win off a bad process teaches us nothing. We reward sound reasoning, run the bets worth running, and judge ourselves by how well we chose, not only by how it landed.

Don't compete, be uncontested.
Competition is a symptom of a weak position. We don't win by racing others down a crowded path, we win by building something no one else can, in a direction no one else is looking. When we find ourselves fighting for scraps, we've made a strategic mistake upstream.

Own it end to end.
There are no bystanders here. We spot what's broken, take full responsibility for a strong result, and see it through. We're self-driven, own our mistakes plainly, and feel deep responsibility for what we're building.

Where we work

We are hiring for this position in our San Francisco office. We are in person 5 days a week.

What we offer

This role offers competitive salary, meaningful equity, and competitive benefits, along with the resources and support to do the best work of your career at a company where the customers are among the most demanding R&D organizations in the world. You'll have unusual freedom to chase hard problems, which also means we'll expect a lot.

Most importantly, you'll help get AI to make real scientific discoveries, one deployment at a time. If you want to do your life's work with us, even if you don't meet every requirement, apply now.

Application process

We have systems in place to detect automated submissions and strongly advise against using bots or automated tools in your application process. Please be human in your approach.

Equal opportunity

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

About This Role

We're building David AI's first Forward Deployed Evals
team. Voice models can only improve on what someone can measure, and most of what matters in voice has never been measured well. This team finds those gaps with our customers and builds the evals to close them.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, Evals
, you'll be the primary partner to a set of customers' research teams. In a typical week, you might spot a regression in the latest model checkpoint and design a targeted eval for it, build it end-to-end, calibrate findings against human ratings, and follow through to ensure the model improves.

This is a builder role that is intentionally cross-functional, requiring you to be capable across GTM, Ops, Product, Research, and Engineering to deliver on outcomes.

In this role, you will

Be the evaluation partner to research teams at the world's leading AI labs: learn what they're trying to fix in their voice models, and find what they haven't thought to measure yet.
Dig into human and automated eval results, pin down exactly where and why a model fails, and decide which failures deserve a dedicated eval.
Go from idea to working eval in days, independently building whatever the problem calls for: human data pipelines, detectors trained on human labels, or synthetic test harnesses.
Make every number defensible: an eval you ship should track what people actually hear, and it should hold up when a senior researcher pushes on it.
Tell research leads what to focus on in their next checkpoint and why, with the data to back it up.
Productize what works, or turn it into a playbook the team can repeat.
Shape how forward deployed evals work at David AI as one of the first people on the team.

Your background looks like

2-7+ years of experience as a technical builder across engineering, product, operations, and research (we're hiring at multiple levels); this might have been as a forward deployed engineer, applied data scientist, ML engineer, product manager, management consultant, or something else entirely.
You're exceptional at building with AI agents, and you've personally built at least one ambitious thing you can walk us through in detail.
You move fast. You solve problems in days that might take someone else a month, and you own ambiguous, high-stakes work end to end.
Strong, demonstrated analytical chops: experiment design, statistics, and knowing whether a metric actually captures what you care about.
Strong customer presence: you have the credibility and clear communication to earn the trust of technical customers and senior stakeholders.
Excited to work in person in San Francisco or New York.

Bonus points if you have

Been a founder, or founding engineer/PM/etc. at a startup.
Experience with speech, audio, or voice models.
Built or published a benchmark you can share with us.
Experience working with human raters, annotation, or data-labeling workflows.
Worked at an AI data or evals company.

Benefits

Unlimited PTO.

FSA & HSA access.
401k access.
Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer – Agentic AI (Accounting & Finance)
added.description:
Agentic AI is moving out of the demo and into the books. Be the engineer who builds it, in the room with the people who will use it.

The mission

Accounting firms close the month, reconcile accounts, and run AP, AR, and general ledger work under deadlines and audit scrutiny that leave no room for an agent that is right only most of the time. A leading financial software platform is placing Forward Deployment pods alongside accounting firms to build AI agents with them on the platform’s own agent-building environment.
As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you meet with the firm, map how the work is done today, and then personally design, build, test, and hand over the agent that does it. You will not hand a design to someone else to implement. Success is a working agent, in the firm’s hands, that its people trust enough to use on Monday morning.
Zensa is the recruiting partner for this search. The engagement is delivered through the professional services organization of a global enterprise-technology provider, following that organization’s AI-native development lifecycle.

At a glance

On site: 3 days per week in Mountain View, CA or Manhattan, NY (living nearby preferred, not required; candidates can travel in)
Customer travel: 1–2 weeks a month to client accounting firms
Type: W2, U.S.-based; 2–3 month engagement
Level: Staff or Senior Consultant
Pay: As per market standards

What you’ll do: you own every stage, end to end

•       Meet and map.
Lead workshops with the firm’s partners, managers, and staff accountants to map how work is done today, including exceptions, hand-offs, controls, and the spreadsheets nobody mentions until you ask. Done: a validated process map and a scoped, testable agent specification the firm agrees to.
•       Design.
Turn a loose request (“automate our reconciliations”) into a concrete agent workflow: tools and APIs, retrieval sources, state, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, guardrails, and failure retry and recovery. Done: a design you can defend line by line, including the trade-offs you rejected.
•       Build.
Write the code yourself on the client’s agent-building platform: tool and API calls, retrieval (RAG), guardrails, and monitoring. Done: a working agent running against representative firm data.
•       Test.
Build test cases from real firm scenarios, exercise edge cases and failure paths, verify retry and recovery, and measure quality before anyone relies on the output. Done: documented coverage and measured quality that meet the agreed bar.
•       Hand over.
Refine the agent from direct user feedback, then hand it over with the documentation the firm and the pod need to run it. Done: adoption by the firm’s team and a clean transfer of ownership.

What you bring

•       Hands-on agent engineering.
You have personally built and run agent workflows using LangGraph, CrewAI, or a similar framework, including tool and API calls, RAG, guardrails, and monitoring.
•       You can walk us through your own build.
Design choices and trade-offs, state handling, failure retry and recovery, and how it was tested. Expect follow-up questions several layers deep.
•       Strong programming.
You write the code, not just the design.
•       Customer discovery.
You have led workshops with business users to map a current process, turned a loose request into a working workflow, and refined agents from user feedback.
•       Fast platform learning.
You will build on the client’s platform, not a stack you already know.
Clear communication.
You can explain a strategy to an engineer and a control exception to an accounting partner with equal precision.

Nice to have

Accounting or finance workflow experience, such as month-end or year-end close, reconciliation, AP/AR, or general ledger work.

Interview Process & Role Expectations

The interview is a technical deep dive on something you built. Pick one agent system from your résumé and be ready to whiteboard its architecture, open the hood on state handling and failure recovery, and explain how it was tested. Say “I” for what you personally built and “we” only for what the team built. Every framework on your résumé is fair game.

We are looking for hands-on engineers who can independently design, build, test, and deploy AI agent solutions while working directly with customers.

This position requires a strong hands-on coding background and a commitment to working onsite three days per week in Mountain View, CA, or Manhattan, NY, along with the specified customer travel requirements. Candidates seeking purely architectural, strategic, program management, or remote-only roles may not be aligned with this opportunity.

Feel free to send me your resume at himanshu@zensa.co

Our technology and team of trusted advisors help members achieve financial independence by taking care of everything from business incorporation to accounting, bookkeeping, tax services, and access to a thriving community, all in one integrated platform. About The Role

This role owns business problems end to end, partnering with leaders across Collective to define the problem, design the process, and build and run the solution. The focus is replacing manual workflows and fragile, one-person tooling with tested, monitored systems, including the integrations and data flows that keep our SaaS tools and warehouse in sync. A big piece is building the platform that lets business teams safely use AI apps and agents, with standard hosting, auth, data access, evals and logging baked in, then shipping the first apps on it. We're looking for someone with 5+ years in solutions architecture, solutions engineering or business systems who has shipped real systems themselves and has hands-on experience with LLMs, agents and MCP, plus SQL, Python and APIs. It's a hands-on, embedded role for someone scrappy and independent who's comfortable with sensitive financial and employee data and would rather ship a durable 80% solution now than wait for perfect.

What You'll Do

Own business problems end to end. Work with leaders across the company to define the problem, design the target process, and then build and run the solution.
Modernize business processes. Replace manual workflows and fragile, hand-maintained tooling with systems that are tested, monitored and documented and don't depend on one person.
Architect integrations and data flows. Design how data moves between our internal SaaS tools and the warehouse so that teams work from accurate, in-sync data.
Evaluate and integrate vendors. Assess build vs. buy, run implementations and integrations, and own their technical architecture.
Build the platform for safe business team usage of AI apps. Set the standard way business-team apps and agents are hosted, authenticated, granted data access, evaluated and logged, so each new tool inherits those controls instead of needing its own review. Build the first apps and agents on it alongside those teams.
Harden the data pipelines business teams depend on. Partner with Data Engineering to make shared pipelines reliable and well owned.
Work embedded in the domains you serve. Act as a dedicated partner who learns each domain, not a ticket queue. Handle sensitive financial and employee data within our security and compliance controls.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent experience (confirm with counsel)
5+ years in solutions architecture, solutions engineering, business systems or a similar technical role that works directly with non-technical stakeholders
A record of turning an ambiguous business problem into a working system that you shipped yourself
Strong stakeholder management: you can explain trade-offs to a business leader and also go deep with an engineer
Experience building and running internal applications in production, including authentication, hosting and deployment
Hands-on experience building with LLMs and AI agents, including tool use, MCP and evaluations
Hands-on with SQL and at least one scripting language, such as Python, plus REST APIs, webhooks and data integration patterns
Experience designing integrations and data flows across SaaS systems and a cloud data warehouse, such as BigQuery
Experience securing systems that handle sensitive financial or employee data, including least-privilege access, audit logging and secrets management

added.title: AI Engineer
added.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Solutions Architecture (SA) organization helps Stripe's most strategic customers design and validate technical solutions that drive their business forward. Within SA, our team builds the tools, workflows, and custom technical assets that make the broader SA org more effective—turning individual ingenuity into org-wide capability.

We are looking for AI Engineers who are energized by working close to the business and the users we serve. You'll operate as an embedded, high-context engineer focused on the highest-leverage opportunities across the SA org—building production-quality tooling, supporting our most strategic engagements, and shipping automation that meaningfully improves how Solutions Architects work every day.

What You'll Do

As an AI Engineer, you'll be embedded directly with the Solutions Architecture team—building alongside them, deeply understanding their workflows, and shipping tools and automation that permanently change how they operate. Your measure of success is SA productivity: the engagements you've accelerated, the workflows you've transformed, and the tools you've built that the org adopts as default.

You'll ship code daily. You'll discover where SAs lose time and build high-impact solutions. You'll take what works for one person and scale it to work for the org. And when our most strategic customer engagements need custom technical assets, you'll build those too.

This is a role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of engineering and business impact—close to customers, close to revenue, and building for people you can see using your work every day.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with Solutions Architects, SA leadership, Product, and Engineering to scope technical work and translate ambiguous business needs into well-defined deliverables
Evaluate and integrate AI capabilities (LLMs, agents, workflow automation) where they provide genuine leverage—not for novelty, but for measurable productivity improvement
Architect and build internal tools, agents, and automated workflows that accelerate SA and manager productivity across technical discovery, solution design, demoing, user engagements, territory/pipeline management, and product interlock
Take high-potential tools and workflows built by SAs and managers and harden them into scalable, maintainable, production-grade solutions
Identify patterns across SA workflows and proactively build solutions that address recurring friction
Build custom demo environments, PoC applications, and technical assets for Stripe's most strategic customer engagements
Document tools, architectures, and usage patterns so others can adopt and extend what you've built
Debug, extend, and maintain backend systems across a variety of codebases and infrastructure

Minimum Requirements

4+ years of experience as an engineer shipping production systems
Strong backend engineering fundamentals: you can debug a failing system, trace issues across services, and reason about data flows
Experience building and deploying AI agents, LLM-powered tools, or workflow automation beyond basic prompt engineering
Experience scoping and delivering work with minimal oversight in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment
Proficiency in at least two of: Ruby, Node.js, Python, or Next.js
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) including deployment, monitoring, and basic DevOps
Experience building internal tools, developer platforms, or workflow automation
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple codebases and technology stacks simultaneously
Hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools in your engineering workflow—you're fluent with AI-assisted development but not dependent on it; you can reason through problems and debug without AI as a crutch
Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders and navigate cross-functional collaboration naturally
Comfort with ambiguity—you can take a loosely-defined business problem, scope the engineering work, and ship iteratively without waiting for a perfect spec

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing systems that non-engineers can build on top of or extend themselves (e.g., platforms, low-code frameworks, template systems)
Experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or GTM Engineering role—or a product engineering role where you worked closely with customers or go-to-market teams
Familiarity with Stripe's products, APIs, or the payments/fintech domain
Experience integrating with third-party platforms (Salesforce, Gong, etc.)
Track record of building tools or systems that were adopted beyond your immediate team
Background in consulting, professional services, or other roles that blend technical depth with business context

Who You Are

Beyond the technical requirements, we're looking for a specific kind of engineer:

You want to be close to the business. You're energized by seeing your work directly impact how a sales team wins a deal or how a customer succeeds.
You're a pragmatic builder. You ship working solutions quickly, iterate based on real usage, and know when "good enough now" beats "perfect later." You'd rather show a working prototype today than present a roadmap deck next quarter.
You're a software engineer by practice. You can architect systems, debug production issues, write clean code, and reason about tradeoffs. AI is a tool in your belt, not a substitute for engineering judgment.
You're a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it generalizes. You think in reusable systems, not one-off scripts.
You thrive without a traditional product team structure. No PRDs landing in your lap, no dedicated PM, no sprint ceremonies. You identify the highest-leverage problem, scope the work, and ship it. You're comfortable trading on-call rotations and rigid processes for autonomy and impact.
You're a strong communicator. You can partner with SAs who are domain experts, understand their workflows deeply enough to build great tools, and explain your technical choices to leadership.

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $172,600 - $258,800. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

added.description:
Plutus is a fast growing company on a mission to democratize access to investing. We're an SEC-registered investment advisor giving everyday investors the kind of portfolio strategy and automated execution that used to be reserved for institutions and the ultra-wealthy. We launched in January, AUM is already in the tens of millions, and we're now looking for a founding machine learning engineer to help take us from v1 to a billion under management by end of year.
We have an enormous amount of customer and portfolio data and not nearly enough of it turned into insight yet. That gap is the job.

Responsibilities

Not cool, useful
- We won’t ask you to prove you used a CNN or transformer model for a job where basic linear regression is sufficient. You will focus on outcomes and product goals without care for the modality!
Turn data into product
- design and build the data pipelines and models that surface insight back to customers, not just dashboards for internal use.
Help drive retention above 98%
- the better we understand what a customer needs and when, the better we keep them. That's on you as much as it's on product.
Be an engineer first, with product sense
- you'll work closely with product and eng, and you should know what's buildable and what isn't, so the things you propose are grounded in what's actually shippable.
Live in the customer's shoes
- regardless of your experience level, the job is finding the gap between what we say the product does and what it actually does, then closing it with data.
Behave like an owner
- the team is small, the stakes are real, and people are here on weekends because they want to see the result of their work, not because anyone's asking them to.

Required

Strong fundamentals in machine learning and applied data science, with real experience taking models from prototype to production
Hands-on experience building and operating data pipelines at scale
Strong software engineering fundamentals - you can write clean, maintainable code, not just notebooks
Extreme ownership and genuine comfort operating in ambiguity at an early-stage startup
Deep curiosity about the customer - you notice when something doesn't quite work, and you can't help but go fix it
Financial motivation is a feature, not a bug, here - but you need to actually believe in the mission, not just be looking for a paycheck

added.title: Principal Engineer, AI/ML
added.description:
Role Summary

We're looking for a Principal Engineer to architect, fine-tune, and deploy on-device small language models (SLMs) for consumer security at scale. You will serve as the technical authority for AI/ML initiatives, driving architecture, model development, optimization, and deployment while collaborating with engineering teams across the organization.

Your core responsibility is building high-performance, privacy-preserving AI models that run directly on user devices (Mac, iOS, Android, Linux). You’ll own model optimization, fine-tuning for tool-use accuracy, evaluation frameworks, and cost-aware deployment strategies. While you won’t own the agent orchestration platform itself, you’ll work closely with it to ensure models behave correctly in multi-turn conversations and make reliable tool-calling decisions. 

This role sits at the intersection of edge ML, applied LLMs, and production engineering. Success requires navigating real-world tradeoffs: latency vs. capability, privacy vs. accuracy, on-device vs. cloud execution, and cost vs. performance. 

This is a Hybrid position located in a hub location of Frisco, TX, San Jose, CA, Newport Beach, CA, or New York, NY. You will be required to be onsite on an as-needed basis, typically 1-4 days per month. We are only considering candidates within a commutable distance to this location and are not offering relocation assistance at this time.

Position Details

About The Role

Design and deploy small language models optimized for on-device inference (Mac, iOS, Android, Linux)
Lead model optimization efforts including quantization, pruning, distillation, and efficient inference pipelines
Fine-tune models to improve tool selection accuracy and conversational behavior in security-focused workflows
Build evaluation frameworks to measure model efficacy, tool-calling accuracy, conversation quality, and safety in production
Create synthetic data and workflow simulations to train and validate security-relevant conversations
Partner closely with agent orchestration systems to optimize multi-turn dialogue behavior and state handling
Implement cost-optimization strategies such as intelligent on-device vs. cloud routing, prompt caching, batching, and token efficiency
Integrate cloud-based LLMs when deeper reasoning or broader context is required
Build production ML systems that detect threats and protect users directly on-device
Set technical standards and architectural direction for AI/ML across the security platform 
Influence engineers, architects, and technical leaders through design reviews, technical guidance, and engineering best practices.
Design and maintain scalable AI evaluation harnesses that enable automated testing, benchmarking, and regression detection across model quality, tool-calling behavior, safety, and production workflows.
Develop red-team testing frameworks and adversarial evaluation methodologies to measure and improve model robustness, security, and resiliency against emerging threat scenarios.
Build reusable AI engineering platforms, tooling, and infrastructure that accelerate model experimentation, evaluation, deployment, and operational monitoring across multiple teams and products.

About You

10+ years of software engineering experience, with 5+ years focused on ML/AI
Proven experience shipping ML models to production with transferrable skills to deploy these on edge or mobile platforms
Experience with conversational AI systems and tool/function-calling architectures
Strong Python and systems programming skills (C++ or Rust) for performance-critical code
Drive cross-functional technical initiatives that span multiple products and engineering organizations.
Deep expertise in model optimization (INT4/INT8 quantization, pruning, distillation)
Hands-on experience with PyTorch and at least one edge deployment framework (TensorFlow Lite, CoreML, ONNX Runtime, or llama.cpp)
Experience building evaluation and benchmarking frameworks for ML systems
Experience applying ML systems in security, safety, or other adversarial domains
Master’s degree in CS, ML, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)  is a plus

Company Overview

McAfee is a leader in personal security for consumers. Focused on protecting people, not just devices, McAfee consumer solutions adapt to users’ needs in an always online world, empowering them to live securely through integrated, intuitive solutions that protects their families and communities with the right security at the right moment.

Company Benefits And Perks

We work hard to embrace diversity and inclusion and encourage everyone at McAfee to bring their authentic selves to work every day. We offer a variety of social programs, flexible work hours and family-friendly benefits to all of our employees.:

Bonus Program
401k Retirement
Medical, Dental, Vision, Basic Life, Short Term Disability and Long-Term Disability Coverage
Paid Parental Leave
Support and Community Involvement
14 Paid Company Holidays
Unlimited Paid Time Off for Exempt Employees
96 Hours of Sick Time and 120 Hours of Vacation for Non-Exempt Employees Accrued Each Year

We're serious about our commitment to diversity which is why McAfee prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation or any other legally protected status.

The anticipated compensation for this position is USD $149,610.00/Yr. - USD $245,790.00/Yr. depending on experience and qualifications.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER, COMPUTER VISION

We are looking for exceptional, driven, adaptable, and resilient senior software engineers who are technical leaders and experts in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and computer vision. As a software engineer on the NDE & Materials Software team, you will accelerate the quality, speed, and efficiency of manufacturing processes at SpaceX by owning end-to-end solutions - from model development to production deployment and monitoring.

Our team is building the next generation of in-process monitoring tools for SpaceX as we develop the Starship, Raptor, and Starlink programs. We deliver high-impact solutions through advanced AI models and scalable simulation with a focus on non-destructive evaluation (NDE) and materials engineering applications. As a technical leader, you will guide the team in applying cutting-edge AI to these manufacturing challenges.

Responsibilities

Lead computer vision model development and deployment for real-time inspection and automated defect recognition in production-scale manufacturing
Architect and implement pipelines for scalable model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and retraining using industry-standard tools like Ray Train/Serve, Kubeflow, Airflow, or equivalent
Develop software to integrate hardware, sensors, and tooling (including sensor fusion) with AI-driven process monitoring systems
Build and optimize data pipelines from production lines, incorporating real-time stream processing and inference
Collaborate with part/process engineers, NDE engineers, and materials scientists to link advanced models and outputs to manufacturing
Lead design and code reviews, technology evaluations, and enforce best practices (e.g., style, CI/CD, accuracy, testability, efficiency, and standards)

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, physics, or related STEM discipline; OR 8+ years of professional experience building and deploying AI software/Machine Learning in lieu of a degree
5+ years of software development experience
3+ years deploying AI models to production environments
3+ years of software engineering experience
3+ years of experience leveraging Python for data analysis

Preferred Skills And Experience

Proven track record as a technical leader in software projects involving AI/ML
Hands-on experience deploying computer vision models for real-time manufacturing inspection and defect detection
Strong development experience in Python and C++ (or similar), with expertise in ML frameworks like PyTorch or JAX
Hands-on experience with computer vision libraries (e.g., OpenCV)Experience fine tuning and adapting state-of-the-art models, such as transformers and vision transformers, to production environments

Experience deploying applications at scale with Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud/edge inference for factory automation

Strong linux experience
Experience applying AI to physics or simulation domains, using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) or surrogate modeling

Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary
Ability to travel to other SpaceX sites as needed (up to 20%)

We’re looking for a Staff AI Developer to lead the design and delivery of AI/ML systems. This role is ideal for an experienced developer who thrives on architectural decisions, can confidently own systems end-to-end, and contributes to technical leadership across the team.

In this role, you will work as a key technical leader on a cross-functional team, defining AI architecture, leading model development and optimization, and solving challenging integration problems. You’ll be joining real, in-flight work where reliability, security, and scalability are critical. You’ll establish engineering standards, raise the bar on how we build AI systems, and contribute to the technical decisions that shape how our AI work scales over time.

Why This Role Matters

At Robots & Pencils, we design AI systems for a human world. Our name says it all. Robots and pencils means engineering paired with creativity, because every agent we ship has to work for real people in real workflows. That balance is baked into how we operate.

Every role here contributes directly to that mission. Here, you shape how AI systems integrate into enterprise operations, how teams move at real velocity, and how products create measurable impact for clients and the people they serve. We ship production-ready AI in 30 to 45 days. That pace demands people who take ownership, lead with craft, and care deeply about what they put their name on.

What You’ll Do

Craft & Delivery

Lead the design and implementation of complex ML/AI systems end-to-end, owning architecture decisions and driving solutions from research through production at scale
Build and evolve scalable ML platforms, pipelines, and infrastructure that support reliable, repeatable model development and deployment across teams
Set the standard for AI-forward engineering, using tools like Claude and Cursor with sophistication and helping the team adopt them effectively

Collaboration & Communication

Partner with product, engineering, and leadership to shape AI strategy and align technical direction with business outcomes
Translate complex AI tradeoffs, risks, and opportunities into clear narratives that drive decision-making across technical and non-technical stakeholders
Lead design reviews and technical discussions, raising the bar for engineering rigor and constructive challenge across the team

Leadership & Influence

Define AI architecture and engineering standards, bringing depth on tradeoffs, long-term implications, and responsible AI practices
Mentor and grow junior and mid-level engineers, multiplying impact through coaching, code reviews, and pairing on hard problems
Take ownership of the most ambiguous and highest-stakes pieces of work, driving them through to production with care for reliability, cost, and safety

What You’ll Bring

7+ years professional software development experience, with 4+ years focused on AI/ML systems in production and deep hands-on experience with generative AI development
Expert software development background (Python or similar) with strong design sensibilities for scalable, maintainable systems
Deep expertise with cloud platforms, including in-depth understanding of AWS services and AWS GenAI offerings

Strong experience with evaluation frameworks and observability tools for LLM apps, including building these capabilities where they don't yet exist

added.title: Senior Applied Scientist, AWS Elemental
added.description:
Description

AWS Elemental builds media services used by broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video. Elemental Inference is the applied machine learning team within that organization. We develop models that understand and transform live and file-based video, producing capabilities such as intelligent reframing, highlight detection, video enhancement, and contextual metadata for advertising and content discovery. Our work reaches customers through the same media workflows that carry major live events, always-on channels, and large on-demand libraries.

As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will develop new machine learning approaches and carry the strongest ideas into production. Current work spans multimodal video, audio, and language models; spatial and temporal understanding; active-speaker and point-of-interest detection; scene retrieval; video super-resolution; and learned methods for improving compression. These problems rarely have a single accepted metric or a ready-made dataset. You will help define the task itself, determine what evidence is needed, and build evaluation methods that reflect the experience of people watching and working with the resulting video.

This role combines applied research with the practical demands of a real-time media service. You will design datasets and objectives, train models at scale, run controlled comparisons, and investigate failures. You will also work closely with engineers to export, optimize, and deploy those models. A result is not finished when it performs well in a notebook. It must preserve its quality after conversion, fit within GPU memory, meet latency and throughput targets, handle the temporal behavior of live video, and operate at a cost customers can sustain.

You will be a technical leader on the team as well as an individual contributor. The role calls for someone who can take an ambiguous customer problem, separate the scientific questions from the engineering constraints, and lead a team toward a defensible answer. You will review experiments and models, mentor other scientists and engineers, and improve the shared methods the team uses for training and evaluation. Strong judgment matters here. So does the ability to explain a complicated result clearly, including its limitations, to people from several disciplines.

We welcome candidates with deep experience in computer vision, multimodal learning, video processing, or related areas. Direct media experience is valuable but not required. A scientist who has solved difficult problems in another field, understands how to test ideas rigorously, and wants to learn the video domain can also succeed in this role.

Key job responsibilities

Lead the formulation of ambiguous video problems into research plans with clear datasets, objectives, baselines, evaluation protocols, and production acceptance criteria.

Develop models for multimodal video understanding and generation, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.

Develop models for multimodal video understanding and description, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.

Build evaluations that measure the behavior customers will see. Depending on the problem, this may include task accuracy, factual support, temporal localization, retrieval quality, perceptual video quality, rate-distortion performance, or human review.

Take models from research code to production-ready artifacts. Partner with engineers on model export, reduced-precision inference, quantization, numerical parity, accelerator-specific optimization, and integration with serving systems and video pipelines.

Balance model quality against latency, throughput, GPU memory, context limits, and operating cost. Diagnose problems across training stability, data quality, precision, compilation, serving, and live temporal behavior.

Build reusable mechanisms for dataset management, experimentation, model comparison, regression detection, and performance measurement rather than solving each research problem in isolation.

Review scientific work and production code. Identify weak comparisons, data leakage, unsupported conclusions, untested edge cases, and operational risks before they reach customers.

Work with product managers, software engineers, and other scientists to make scope and design decisions. Use evidence to resolve disagreement and communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what further work is worth doing.

Mentor scientists and engineers in experimental design, machine learning methods, video evaluation, and production ML practices.

Contribute applied research through internal technical reports, patents, and publications at appropriate conferences or workshops.

About The Team

AWS Elemental provides a portfolio of cloud media services built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. Our technology supports some of the world's largest live broadcasts as well as 24/7 channels and on-demand content. The broader organization brings together expertise in video coding, image processing, distributed systems, advertising, and the operational demands of professional media.

Elemental Inference applies machine learning across that video pipeline. The team works on video understanding and enhancement, contextual metadata, smart composition, event detection, retrieval, and compression. Some projects use large multimodal models that combine video, audio, and language. Others use specialized temporal or spatial models designed for a narrow task and a strict real-time budget. We choose the approach that fits the customer problem rather than forcing every problem into the same model family.

Scientists on the team own more than model architecture. They build and govern datasets, develop annotation methods, train on distributed GPU infrastructure, and create evaluations that can reveal where a model succeeds or fails. They compare internal models with external alternatives and track accuracy, perceptual quality, latency, memory use, and cost. When a model is ready to ship, scientists work with engineers to convert it into a verified production artifact and integrate it into the inference service or the underlying video-processing engine.

Basic Qualifications

PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

added.description:
Description -

Senior Data Scientist – Edge AI Platforms & Systems Analytics

Job Summary

The Commercial Systems Software Engineering organization is developing next-generation AI software platforms that enable intelligent, secure, and scalable experiences across client and edge computing environments.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Data Scientist to lead the development of the data and analytics foundation supporting strategic AI software initiatives. This role will be responsible for integrating data from a wide range of software, hardware, AI, telemetry, performance, and business systems, enabling data-driven decision making across engineering, product, and program management organizations.

The successful candidate will combine expertise in data engineering, machine learning, analytics, experimentation, and statistical modeling to deliver insights that improve platform performance, software quality, customer experiences, and business outcomes. This role will work closely with software architects, engineering teams, technical program managers, and leadership teams to establish scalable data pipelines, develop predictive models, and create actionable insights that guide technology and investment decisions.

Responsibilities

Design and implement scalable data architectures that support multiple software platform initiatives.
Integrate data across software telemetry, hardware platforms, AI workloads, validation systems, engineering tools, benchmarking environments, and business systems.
Develop and maintain reliable data pipelines, data models, transformation processes, and reporting frameworks.
Define data governance, quality, lineage, security, and lifecycle management standards.
Build machine learning models that identify performance trends, anomalies, optimization opportunities, and operational risks.
Apply advanced statistical methods to understand workload behavior, system utilization, software effectiveness, and customer usage patterns.
Develop workload characterization models and comparative analyses across different platform configurations and operating conditions.
Build predictive models for performance, reliability, capacity planning, and system behavior.
Design and execute experiments that validate hypotheses and measure the effect of software or platform changes.
Develop executive dashboards, scorecards, and visualizations that provide meaningful visibility into platform health and key business metrics.
Partner with engineering teams to translate data-driven insights into product and platform improvements.
Present analytical findings and recommendations to technical teams, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
Drive data literacy and analytics best practices across the organization.
Mentor engineers and analysts on machine learning, experimentation methodologies, and data science practices.

Education & Experience Recommended

Four-year or Graduate Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
Typically 8+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, advanced analytics, data engineering, or related technical disciplines.
Proven experience building production-scale analytics platforms, data pipelines, and machine learning solutions.
Experience working with large and complex datasets generated from software systems, AI platforms, cloud environments, or connected devices.
Demonstrated ability to lead analytics initiatives across multiple engineering and business organizations.
Experience supporting data-driven decision making at both technical and leadership levels.

Core Data Science & Analytics Expertise

Strong foundation in machine learning, predictive analytics, statistical modeling, forecasting, optimization, clustering, classification, regression, and anomaly detection.
Experience applying supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques to solve complex business and engineering problems.
Deep understanding of statistical analysis, experimental design, hypothesis testing, model evaluation, and validation methodologies.
Ability to build analytical frameworks that support decision making under uncertainty.
Experience measuring model performance, monitoring drift, and ensuring analytical rigor and reproducibility.
Familiarity with Generative AI, large language models, AI inference workflows, and AI workload characterization.

Data Engineering & Platform Skills

Advanced proficiency in Python, SQL, and modern data science libraries and frameworks.
Experience designing and implementing large-scale data pipelines and automated data-processing systems.
Strong knowledge of data architecture, data modeling, ETL/ELT processes, and data integration techniques.
Experience with technologies such as Spark, Databricks, Kafka, Airflow, Snowflake, or equivalent platforms.
Experience working with cloud-based analytics and data platforms.
Familiarity with MLOps practices including model deployment, monitoring, versioning, automation, and lifecycle management.
Understanding of telemetry systems, observability frameworks, APIs, and distributed architectures.

AI, Edge Computing & Systems Knowledge

Understanding of AI and machine learning deployment across client, edge, and cloud environments.
Familiarity with AI inference workflows and resource utilization across CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, storage, networking, and cloud resources.
Experience analyzing system telemetry, performance data, workload behavior, and resource utilization patterns.
Knowledge of software performance measurement, benchmarking methodologies, and workload characterization techniques.
Understanding of platform software architectures and modern software development practices.

Leadership & Communication Skills

Strong problem-solving and analytical reasoning skills.
Ability to transform complex datasets into actionable business and technical recommendations.
Experience developing executive dashboards, presentations, scorecards, and decision-support materials.
Proven ability to communicate findings to technical audiences as well as senior leadership.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain sophisticated analytical concepts clearly.
Demonstrated ability to influence decisions through data-driven insights.
Ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, product management, program management, and business teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting AI, edge computing, client platforms, enterprise systems, or software infrastructure programs.
Experience with telemetry analytics, workload optimization, performance engineering, benchmarking, or predictive maintenance solutions.
Familiarity with Power BI, Tableau, Grafana, Kibana, or other visualization and reporting platforms.
Experience analyzing large-scale system, device, or application data.
Experience working with external technology partners and ecosystem providers.

Impact & Scope

Provides the data, analytics, and machine learning foundation that enables engineering teams and business leaders to make informed decisions across strategic AI software initiatives. Influences platform design, software optimization, investment priorities, product strategy, and executive decision-making through scalable analytics and actionable insights.

Complexity

Works across large-scale datasets spanning software platforms, AI workloads, system telemetry, cloud services, engineering environments, and business systems. Requires balancing data engineering, machine learning, experimentation, analytics, and executive communications while supporting multiple concurrent initiatives and stakeholders.
